messages:
emma: quick alert - us-west1 local NVMe iops jumped to ~220k for 18m, GPU attach failures and pod pending rising. infra-bot already fired.
infra-bot: [ALERT] local_nvme_iops > 200000 (us-west1)  18m. dash: /dash/local-iops-us-west1. runbook: /runbooks/attach-backpressure.md
raj: seeing a clear overlap: scheduled scrub window + nightly batch reclaim + surge of image pulls. pending GPUs ~95.
oscar: scrub rollout yesterday bumped concurrency to 14 to clear backlog. that likely saturated controllers.
bea: can we throttle scrub for region only? last time reducing to 4 helped. we should also flip image-cache warm mode.
emma: agreed. plan: 1) set SCRUB_CONC=4 for us-west1, 2) disable aggressive trim for 40m, 3) scale cleaner replicas to 1. scope to region.
raj: commands (scoped):
```
kubectl set env deployment/cleaner CLEANER_SCRUB_CONCURRENCY=4 -n infra-us-west1
kubectl set env deployment/cleaner ENABLE_AGGRESSIVE_TRIM=false -n infra-us-west1
kubectl scale deployment/cleaner --replicas=1 -n infra-us-west1
```
I can apply now.
[oscar thumbs-up reaction]
infra-bot: [ACTION] cleaner env patched by raj (CLEANER_SCRUB_CONCURRENCY=4)
raj: patch applied. monitoring iops.
bea: flipping local-image-cache to warm-cache and bumping cache-size by +30% to cut read amplification.
emma: early signal: iops dropped 220k -> 70k within 9m, attach pending down 95 -> 11. good.
cost-bot: note - if we need to spill traffic to eu-west2, estimated additional cost ~$130/hr if we route 15% of new GPU launches. Approve for emergency 2h? finance auto-approve threshold set to $200/hr.
oscar: we probably won't need spill now. keep it as backup.
bea: follow-ups: create an adaptive-scrub RFC, add region-scoped concurrency knobs to cleaner, and expand image cache policy. filing tickets.
emma: scheduling retro with scheduler and janitor owners at 09:30 tomorrow. leaving sensitivity alerts high for 3h. great fast work. :thumbsup:
raj: will revert aggressive-trim flag after backlog drops and confirm no attach regressions. closing thread unless we see more failures.
